items.title: Live: Bank Nifty tops 64,000 for the 1st time; Nifty, Sensex surges 2% this week | Closing Bell
items.description: Sensex and Nifty extended gains for a second straight session on Friday, ending the week with their fourth consecutive weekly gain. Both indices surged over 2% for the week, and the Nifty has rallied around 14% in the last four weeks. The Sensex jumped about 800 points and erased its opening loss, while the Nifty 50 hit a nine-month high above the 25,700 mark. The Bank Nifty also scaled a fresh record high, topping 64,500. Volatility rose in an upbeat market, with the VIX jumping 8%. Midcaps ended in the green, the IT index snapped a three-day losing streak, and realty and auto stocks saw decent buying, while consumer durable and metal stocks stayed under pressure. Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare and Axis Bank were the top Nifty gainers, while Titan, Tata Steel and NTPC were the top losers. The rupee touched a seven-month high, breaching below the 93 mark against the dollar, while gold slid 4% and silver tumbled 6% on MCX. Watch Closing Bell for a complete wrap of the day’s market action, sector trends and the stocks that moved the most.

items.title: Will the FM Cut Capital Gains Tax in the Budget? Experts on FPIs & Double Taxation | Centre Point
items.description: On this episode of Centre Point, we bring together Sunil Badala, Partner and Head of Tax at KPMG in India, and Sameer Gupta, National Tax Leader at EY India, to debate one of the biggest questions for Indian markets: should foreign portfolio investors get more favourable tax treatment? FPIs have pulled out around $20 billion from Indian equities so far in 2026, despite a strong rebound in November, and the capital gains tax debate is back in focus. India levies 20% on short-term and 12.5% on long-term gains, which works out to roughly 13% to 21.84% for FPIs once surcharge and cess are included. Most major global markets, including the US, UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Germany and the UAE, charge no capital gains tax on foreign investors. Our guests weigh in on whether this gap is hurting FPI sentiment, how the tax burden compares between FPIs and local investors, and whether STT and capital gains tax together amount to double taxation of equities. They also discuss the case for abolishing capital gains tax, the options the government has to rationalise it, and whether the Finance Minister could announce relief in the upcoming Budget.

items.description: Wall Street’s slide extended overnight, with the Dow ending below 50,000 for the first time since June, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq losing about 2% each, and the volatility index at its highest since March. Asian markets followed, with the Nikkei and Kospi sharply lower, and GIFT Nifty is hinting at a gap-down start for Indian equities. Anthropic’s blockbuster Nasdaq debut, which briefly touched a $2 trillion valuation before pulling back, did little to lift AI sentiment. On the commodities front, Brent crude hovers near $93 and is set for a third weekly fall, while gold and silver remain close to 14-month lows. Back home, the Nifty recovered 410 points from its intraday low on Thursday, the Bank Nifty hit a record above 63,000, and FIIs were net buyers while DIIs sold. Watch Opening Bell for all the pre-market cues, the global setup and the key stocks in the news before the market opens.
